description: Welcome to NeoFrontier! We are a multidisciplinary group tackling the "Earth Analogs for Moon & Mars" challenge. Our mission is to go beyond simple visual similarities and build a data-driven, interactive solution—such as a mapping application or a machine learning tool—that systematically identifies and characterizes terrestrial analogs using NASA's open datasets.
summary: NeoFrontier is an interactive 3D platform for exploring candidate regions on the Moon and Mars and finding Earth environments with comparable characteristics. Its Python data pipeline samples public planetary and Earth datasets, derives site metrics such as relief, safe slope, solar exposure, albedo, terrain-hazard proxies, soil-property estimates, and ice-related indicators, and ranks Earth grid cells with a configurable similarity model. A Three.js globe lets users select planetary targets, inspect coordinates and factor-level provenance, and compare results with terrestrial analogs. The project supports education and early-stage field research by helping teams identify real places on Earth for environmental simulation and comparative study. Data coverage varies by location; measured, model-derived, and proxy values are labeled separately. Results are exploratory and are not certified landing-safety recommendations.
details:
NeoFrontier combines a Three.js 3D globe with a Python open-data pipeline. Users explore Earth, Moon, and Mars targets, review site factors and their provenance, and compare planetary candidates with ranked terrestrial locations. The pipeline samples public datasets, derives terrain metrics, records whether values are measured, calculated, or estimated, and searches an Earth grid using a configurable similarity model. Factors include relief, safe slope, sunlight, albedo, terrain-hazard estimates, soil-property proxies, and ice, snow, or permafrost indicators. Moon and Mars also have body-specific context, such as Earth visibility and atmospheric density.

The project uses JavaScript, HTML/CSS, Three.js, Vite, Python, NumPy, Rasterio, pyproj, Requests, and public raster and API data. It aims to help educators and researchers identify terrestrial field locations for comparative studies and natural-environment simulation. Some locations have incomplete data, and some values are proxies; the results are exploratory, not operational landing assessments.

AI disclosure: OpenAI Codex assisted with code and documentation and with approximate proxy calculations and data. The project labels estimates with their methods and limitations. No AI-generated images, video, or audio were used in the work done with this assistant.
dataRefs: NASA Solar System Treks — Moon and Mars imagery
LRO LOLA — lunar illumination, Earth visibility, and polar-shadow products
MGS MOLA — Mars global elevation model, distributed by USGS Astrogeology
Mars Odyssey GRS — water-equivalent hydrogen data
NASA Earthdata GIBS — Earth imagery and terrain visual resources
NASA Artemis III candidate landing regions
